fact: Chad is one of six CEMAC states covered by GIMAC's interoperable QR Code standard, validated by the UMAC ministerial committee in April 2026 and launched on 29 July 2026 over GIMACPAY, in service since 2021.
Chad is one of the CEMAC states on GIMACPAY, the regional platform that processed 20.3 million transactions worth FCFA 863 billion in 2025, with the BEAC among its 153 participants.

Chad's payment-institution licences are granted by the Central African Banking Commission (Cobac) under the CEMAC regulation of 21 December 2018; Airtel Money (2023), Konoom (2025) and Moov Money Tchad (2026) hold one.

AfricaNenda says the regional central bank BEAC, whose rules apply to the six CEMAC states including Chad, regulates payment market structures including technical approvals and authorisations of payment solutions.
AfricaNenda says BEAC owns 99.2% of GIMACPAY, is its overseer and settlement agent, and the switch serves payment providers in Chad.
AfricaNenda says GIMACPAY, live since July 2020, provides interoperable payment services to providers in the six CEMAC states including Chad.
Chad's mobile money providers are interoperable via GIMACPAY in the CEMAC zone, per Tchadinfos.
BEAC, the central bank of the CEMAC states, joined the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS), per Afreximbank on 9 July 2026, with CEMAC banks to be connected by end-2026.
